To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Islamic indexes are recipient of spillovers of volatility from conventional indexes in both majority Muslim countries (Indonesia and Malaysia) and in minority Muslim countries (China and Pakistan) and Islamic indexes performed comparatively well in terms of mean return during crises.

Islamic indexes have a higher degree of volatility spillover in Muslim minority countries (India and China) and in Muslim majority countries (Indonesia and Malaysia) than in Muslim majority countries.
Islamic indexes are not a safe haven in normal times but are a safe haven in crisis times in countries where Muslims constitute the majority.
